question: Chios cut off from the skies for four months during implementation of cofinanced project

The Hellenic Civil Aviation Authority has announced the suspension of scheduled flights and the closure of the runway at Chios’s only airport from 15 November 2026 to 15 March 20271, prompting a chorus of opposition from the Municipal Council and protests from local bodies2. For a large, outlying island, being cut off from air travel for months entails severe socioeconomic costs.

Chios’s healthcare associations (medical, pharmaceutical and dental) warn of the consequences for access to healthcare services, especially for patients requiring frequent travel3. The envisaged helicopter air ambulance services are no substitute for the regular transport of patients and their carers.

Instead of benefiting the islanders, the improvement project risks depriving them of basic transport infrastructure for months. Phase II is co-financed through the ‘Transport 2021-2027’ programme, with EUR 21.5 million in eligible public expenditure4. Article 174 TFEU sets out that special attention must be paid to island regions5. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Does it consider a four-month interruption of the regular air services of an outlying island to be compatible with the objectives of EU co-financing?
Will it immediately request technical substantiation for the timeline and an examination of solutions that limit the duration of the suspension to what is strictly necessary?
Will it investigate whether the competent authorities have put in place adequate measures for access to healthcare, transport services and limiting the impact on residents?
